description: SFT training prompts for injector scenarios. Uses pre-numbered {sentences} input and outputs a single modified sentence in compact format (N. <modified sentence>). Aligned with error_injection_prompts_v4.json used in self-play RL.

injector_error.description: Injector error: given numbered sentences, introduce a subtle clinical error in one sentence
injector_error.system_prompt:
You are a clinical note editor.

Introduce ONE subtle clinical error by changing 1-3 words in one sentence. Leave all other sentences unchanged.

Output format: the changed sentence number and modified text on a single line.
Example: 5. Patient was prescribed aspirin for bacterial infection.
injector_error.user_template:
Inject a {error_type} error into one sentence of this note by changing 1-3 words.

{sentences}

Reason about the cognitive trap, then output the changed sentence in the format:
N. <modified sentence>

injector_benign.description: Injector benign: given numbered sentences, make a safe surface change to one sentence
injector_benign.system_prompt:
You are a clinical note editor.

Make a benign change that preserves all clinical meaning. Change only the surface wording of ONE sentence, not the medical facts.

Output format: the changed sentence number and modified text on a single line.
Example: 3. Patient was diagnosed with petit mal seizure.

change_type_descriptions.pseudo_factual: Replace a medical term with an equivalent synonym (e.g., "absence seizure" → "petit mal seizure").
change_type_descriptions.temporal_rephrasing: Rephrase a time expression keeping the same duration (e.g., "6-month history" → "180-day history").
change_type_descriptions.equivalent_citation: Replace a drug or procedure name with its class or equivalent (e.g., "metoprolol" → "beta-blocker").

output_format.description: Injector outputs a single line: the 1-indexed sentence number followed by the modified sentence text.
examples: 3. Patient was diagnosed with petit mal seizure.
7. Prescribed a beta-blocker for rate control.
